newsitem.title: USA: Rexene holders pleased by company response.
newsitem.headline: Rexene holders pleased by company response.

text.p: Wyser-Pratte & Co Inc and Spear, Leeds & Kellogg on Friday said they were pleased that Rexene Corp would entertain bids of $16 a share.
Still, they said the company's push to have a transaction completed within 60 days was unreasonable.

"We are gratified that the board of Rexene Corp is beginning to respond to shareholder pressure to sell the company for $16 per share and is no longer insisting that the company be purchased through a tender offer," Wyser-Pratte President Guy Wyser-Pratt and Fred Kambeitz, the managing director of Spear, said in a joint statement.
"Although this is a good first step, Rexene's board must be aware that 60 days is an arbitrary and unreasonable short period of time to complete a cash merger transaction ..." they added.

Rexene, which has rejected an unsolicited $16 per share cash offer from Huntsman Corp, is urging shareholders to reject a proposal by Wyser-Pratte to call a special meeting and to install a new board.
Wyser-Pratte and Spear own a combined 1.9 million shares, or about 10.1 percent, of Rexene's outstanding common stock.

On Thursday, Rexene said it thought the $16-per-share offer does not fully reflect the long-term prospects of the company. However, it said it would not oppose a fully financed cash offer to acquire the company at $16 a share.
Rexene also said it would take steps to invalidate its poison pill anti-takeover plan if it received an offer that met its conditions.
In opposing the Wyser-Pratte slate, Rexene said Wyser-Pratte directors had no experience with the company and would be forced to sell it at a low price if a $16-per-share deal did not materialize.
